topic.title: NVIDIA Driver 621.24 – Samsung QE55Q6FNATXXH TV no longer detected via HDMI (RTX 5070)

firstComment.body:
Hello NVIDIA community,
I would like to report a display detection issue introduced with NVIDIA GeForce driver version 621.24.
After updating from driver 621.14 to 621.24, my Samsung QE55Q6FNATXXH television completely disappeared from Windows 11 display settings.

System configuration:
GPU: MSI GeForce RTX 5070 GAMING TRIO OC 12GB
OS: Windows 11 2H2
Problematic driver: NVIDIA 621.24
Previous working driver: NVIDIA 621.14
Main monitor: Dell S2721DGF (2560×1440, 165Hz, DisplayPort)
TV: Samsung QE55Q6FNATXXH (HDMI)
Connection: Direct HDMI connection from RTX 5070 to Samsung TV, without adapters or AV receivers.
HAGS: Enabled
Variable Refresh Rate: Enabled

Problem description:
With driver 621.14, both displays worked correctly.
Immediately after updating to driver 621.24, the Samsung television stopped being detected.
Restarting the NVIDIA graphics driver using Win + Ctrl + Shift + B does not resolve the issue.
Install NVIDIA driver 621.14 and verify that both displays work.
Update the driver to version 621.24.
Confirmed workaround
Reinstalling NVIDIA driver 621.14 immediately restores Samsung TV detection and normal operation.
This strongly suggests a regression in driver 621.24, potentially related to HDMI display detection or EDID communication.
I have also submitted a report through NVIDIA's official driver feedback form.
I would appreciate it if NVIDIA could investigate this issue and address it in a future driver release.
Has anyone else experienced similar HDMI detection problems with Samsung televisions after installing driver 621.24?
